claim: Signal recognition particles (SRPs) are universal ribonucleoprotein complexes found in all three domains of life.
source: Signal recognition particles (SRPs) are universal ribonucleoprotein complexes found in all three domains of life that direct the cellular traffic and secretion of proteins.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about SRPs being present across all domains of life.

claim: Signal recognition particles direct the cellular traffic and secretion of proteins.
source: Signal recognition particles (SRPs) are universal ribonucleoprotein complexes found in all three domains of life that direct the cellular traffic and secretion of proteins.
evidence: This describes the established functional role of SRPs in protein trafficking.

claim: SRP complexes consist of SRP proteins and a single, highly structured SRP RNA.
source: These complexes consist of SRP proteins and a single, highly structured SRP RNA.
evidence: This describes the known composition of SRP complexes.

claim: Canonical SRP RNA genes have not been identified for some Thermoproteus species.
source: Canonical SRP RNA genes have not been identified for some Thermoproteus species even though they contain SRP19 and SRP54 proteins.
evidence: This is an observation about the absence of identified canonical SRP RNA genes in certain species.

claim: Some Thermoproteus species contain SRP19 and SRP54 proteins.
source: Canonical SRP RNA genes have not been identified for some Thermoproteus species even though they contain SRP19 and SRP54 proteins.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the presence of specific SRP proteins in Thermoproteus species.

claim: Genome rearrangement events in Thermoproteus tenax created a permuted SRP RNA gene.
source: Here, we show that genome rearrangement events in Thermoproteus tenax created a permuted SRP RNA gene.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on genomic analysis.

claim: The 5'- and 3'-termini of the T. tenax SRP RNA are located close to a functionally important loop present in all known SRP RNAs.
source: The 5'- and 3'-termini of this SRP RNA are located close to a functionally important loop present in all known SRP RNAs.
evidence: This describes the structural organization of the permuted SRP RNA based on sequence analysis.

claim: RNA-Seq analyses revealed that the termini of T. tenax SRP RNA are ligated together to generate circular SRP RNA molecules.
source: RNA-Seq analyses revealed that these termini are ligated together to generate circular SRP RNA molecules that can bind to SRP19 and SRP54.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on RNA-Seq experimental data.

claim: Circular SRP RNA molecules can bind to SRP19 and SRP54.
source: RNA-Seq analyses revealed that these termini are ligated together to generate circular SRP RNA molecules that can bind to SRP19 and SRP54.
evidence: This is a finding based on binding assay experiments described in the methods.

claim: The circularization site of T. tenax SRP RNA is processed by the tRNA splicing endonuclease.
source: The circularization site is processed by the tRNA splicing endonuclease.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental cleavage assays with the enzyme.

claim: The tRNA splicing machinery has moonlighting activity that permits the permutation of the SRP RNA.
source: This moonlighting activity of the tRNA splicing machinery permits the permutation of the SRP RNA and creates highly stable and functional circular RNA molecules.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings showing tRNA splicing endonuclease processing SRP RNA.

claim: The tRNA splicing machinery creates highly stable and functional circular RNA molecules.
source: This moonlighting activity of the tRNA splicing machinery permits the permutation of the SRP RNA and creates highly stable and functional circular RNA molecules.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the stability and functionality data of circular SRP RNA.

claim: T. tenax Kra1 (DSM 2078) cells were grown heterotrophically in Thermoproteus medium.
source: Cells of T. tenax Kra1 (DSM 2078) were a kind gift of R. Hensel (Essen) and grown heterotrophically in Thermoproteus medium (Brock et al., 1972).
evidence: This describes the experimental growth conditions used in the study, with citation to the medium protocol.

claim: T. tenax total RNA (>200 nt) and small RNAs (<200 nt) were isolated using the mirVanaTM miRNA Isolation Kit.
source: For the preparation of T. tenax total (>200 nt) and small RNAs (<200 nt), 0.1 g pelleted cells were lysed by homogenization and the RNA was subsequently isolated using the mirVanaTM miRNA Isolation Kit (Ambion, Germany) according to the manufacturer's instructions.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used for RNA isolation.

claim: SRP S-domain RNA constructs (WT, Open, GNAR, h8b) were generated using two forward and reverse complementary DNA oligonucleotides with 15 bases overhangs.
source: To generate the SRP S-domain RNA constructs (WT, Open, GNAR, h8b), two forward and reverse complementary DNA oligonucleotides with 15 bases overhangs were synthesized (Eurofins MWG Operon, Germany Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This describes the experimental method for generating RNA constructs.

claim: The oligonucleotides for SRP S-domain constructs were cloned upstream of a T7 RNA polymerase promoter into pUC19.
source: The oligonucleotides were phosphorylated, hybridized and cloned upstream of a T7 RNA polymerase promoter into pUC19.
evidence: This describes the cloning strategy used in the experimental procedure.

claim: The full-length SRP RNA gene was synthesized with a T7 RNA polymerase promoter and cloned into pMA-RQ.
source: The full-length SRP RNA gene was synthesized with a T7 RNA polymerase promoter and cloned into pMA-RQ (Life Technologies, Germany).
evidence: This describes the experimental method for generating the full-length SRP RNA construct.

claim: SRP and S-domain RNA constructs were prepared by run-off transcription using T7 RNA polymerase at 37°C for 4 hr.
source: The SRP and S-domain RNA constructs were prepared by run-off transcription of 1 µg linearized plasmid as template DNA in a buffer containing 40 mM HEPES/KOH pH 8.0, 22 mM MgCl2, 5 mM dithiothreitol (DTT), 1 mM spermidine, 4 mM of ATP, CTP, GTP and UTP, 20 U RNase inhibitor and 1 µg T7 RNA polymerase at 37°C for 4 hr.
evidence: This describes the in vitro transcription protocol used in the study.

claim: T. tenax small RNA preparations were treated with T4 polynucleotide kinase (T4 PNK) to ensure proper adapter ligation of RNA termini.
source: Preparations of T. tenax small RNAs were treated with T4 polynucleotide kinase (T4 PNK, Ambion) to ensure proper adapter ligation of RNA termini.
evidence: This describes the RNA-Seq library preparation method.

claim: cDNA libraries were prepared according to the TruSeq Small RNA Library Protocol and sequenced using HiSeq2000 technology.
source: The cDNA libraries were prepared according to the TruSeq Small RNA Library Protocol (Illumina) and sequenced using HiSeq2000 technology (Illumina) at the Max-Planck Genome Centre (Cologne).
evidence: This describes the sequencing methodology used in the study.

claim: Sequencing data processing and analyses were performed using CLC Genomics Workbench 8.
source: Sequencing data processing and analyses were performed using CLC Genomics Workbench 8 (Qiagen, Germany).
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics tool used for data analysis.

claim: The trimmed sequences were mapped to the T. tenax reference genome (FN869859).
source: The trimmed sequences were mapped to the T. tenax reference genome (FN869859) using default settings (mismatch cost set to 4).
evidence: This describes the sequence mapping procedure used in the analysis.

claim: The T. tenax RNA-Seq data is available at Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE72127).
source: The T. tenax RNA-Seq data is available at Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE72127, [http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE72127]).
evidence: This provides the data repository accession number for the RNA-Seq data.

claim: Full length SRP RNA transcript was circularized using 5'-dephosphorylation, 5'-phosphorylation, and T4 RNA ligase 1 ligation.
source: To obtain a circular SRP RNA control, full length SRP RNA transcript was 5'-dephosphorylated for 6 hr at 37°C using alkaline phosphatase (NEB) and the reaction was stopped by heating for 10 min at 65°C. Then, the RNA was 5'-phosphorylated using T4 PNK (NEB) and ATP for 1 hr at 37°C and ligated using T4 RNA ligase 1 (NEB) for 1 hr at 37°C.
evidence: This describes the experimental method for generating circular SRP RNA controls.

claim: Hybridization for Northern blot was performed at 42°C for 18 hr in ULTRAhyb-Oligo buffer with two 5'-labeled probes complementary to different regions in the SRP S-domain.
source: Hybridization was performed at 42°C for 18 hr in ULTRAhyb-Oligo buffer (Ambion) with two 5'-labeled probes (the label was added using T4 PNK [NEB] and γ-[32P]-ATP [5000 ci/mmol, Hartmann Analytic]) that were complementary to different regions in the SRP S-domain (42 or 45-mer probe, Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This describes the Northern blot hybridization protocol used in the study.

claim: The T. tenax genes srp19 (TTX_2083) and srp54 (TTX_0615) were cloned into pET20b creating a fusion with a C-terminal 6× His-tag.
source: The T. tenax genes srp19 (TTX_2083) and srp54 (TTX_0615) were cloned into pET20b creating a fusion with a C-terminal 6× His-tag.
evidence: This describes the cloning strategy for recombinant protein production.

claim: SRP19-His protein was heat-precipitated at 70°C for 30 min.
source: The protein was heat-precipitated (30 min, 70°C) and centrifuged (14,000 × g, 30 min, 4°C).
evidence: This describes a step in the protein purification protocol.

claim: SRP19-His protein was purified by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography and eluted at 400 mM imidazole.
source: The SRP19-His protein was further purified by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography (HisTrap HP, GE Healthcare) and eluted with a linear imidazole gradient (0–500 mM) at 400 mM imidazole using a FPLC Äkta system (GE Healthcare).
evidence: This describes the protein purification method and elution conditions.

claim: SRP54-His was purified using Ni-NTA affinity chromatography followed by HiTrap Heparin Sepharose HP column chromatography, eluting at 650 mM NaCl.
source: Protein fractions were dialysed in buffer 3 (50 mM Tris/HCl pH 7.5, 10% glycerol, 1 mM DTT) and purified over a HiTrap Heparin Sepharose HP column (GE Healthcare) eluting with a linear salt gradient (0–1 M) at 650 mM NaCl.
evidence: This describes the two-step protein purification protocol for SRP54.

claim: The formation of SRP RNA-protein complexes was tested using a DEAE-Sepharose assay as described earlier.
source: The formation of SRP RNA-protein complexes was tested using a DEAE-Sepharose assay as described earlier (Bhuiyan, 2000; Gowda, 1997).
evidence: This describes the binding assay method with citations to previous protocols.

claim: 2 µM of the SRP S-domain RNA constructs were folded in binding buffer, heated for 10 min at 65°C and cooled down to room temperature for 1 hr before protein addition.
source: 2 µM of the SRP S-domain RNA constructs (WT, Open, GNAR, h8b) were folded in 55 µl binding buffer (50 mM Tris/HCl pH 8, 300 mM KOAc, 5 mM MgCl2, 1 mM DTT), heated for 10 min at 65°C and cooled down to room temperature for 1 hr.
evidence: This describes the RNA folding protocol used in binding assays.

claim: The binding efficiency of SRP RNA-protein complexes was tested in three independent experiments.
source: The binding efficiency was tested in three independent experiments.
evidence: This describes the experimental replication performed for binding assays.

claim: The T. tenax genes TTX_1594 (catalytic subunit) and TTX_1893 (structural subunit) encode the tRNA splicing endonuclease.
source: The T. tenax genes TTX_1594 (catalytic subunit) and TTX_1893 (structural subunit) were cloned together into pETDuet-1 and the protein was purified as described earlier(Zwieb, 2005).
evidence: This is inferred from the context that these genes encode the tRNA splicing endonuclease subunits, with citation to previous work.

claim: The tRNA splicing endonuclease cell lysate was heat-precipitated at 80°C for 30 min.
source: The cell lysate was heat-precipitated (30 min, 80°C) and centrifuged (14,000 × g, 30 min, 4°C).
evidence: This describes a step in the enzyme purification protocol.

claim: RNA cleavage assays were performed with 1–1000 nM purified splicing endonuclease and 2 nM of 5'-labeled RNA at 60°C for 20 min.
source: 1–1000 nM purified splicing endonuclease was incubated with 2 nM of 5'-labeled RNA in nuclease buffer (40 mM Tris/HCl pH 8, 2 mM MgCl2, 1 mM EDTA) at 60°C for 20 min.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions for RNA cleavage assays.
